newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-RAFTER BEATS PIOLINE, HEAT IN DAVIS CUP TIE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RAFTER BEATS PIOLINE, HEAT IN DAVIS CUP TIE.

text.p: Patrick Rafter staged a remarkable comeback in blistering heat on Friday to defeat Cedric Pioline in five sets and give Australia an early advantage over holders France in their Davis Cup first round tie.
Rafter came back from two-sets-to-love down to win 3-6 6-7 (5-7) 6-4 7-5 6-4 in four hours and 15 minutes and give Australia an unexpected 1-0 lead.
Rafter, ranked 64 in the world compared with Pioline's 26, was erratic in the early stages of the match and fell behind to the more consistent play of the Frenchman.
While occasionally brilliant, Rafter was also error-prone.
In the second set the Australian raced to a 5-1 lead, only to lose his next two service games through a string of double faults and other unforced errors.
Pioline, whose unerring backhand proved his greatest weapon, fought back to force a tie-break, which he won 7-5 after trailing Rafter 1-4.

Rafter however proved more able to cope with the hot conditions on the White City grass courts, shrugging off the disappointment of the first two sets to break Pioline's serve in the ninth game of the third.
That proved decisive for the Australian, with the French number one appearing to struggle with the 36 degrees Celsius (97 Fahrenheit) heat the longer the match continued.
Pioline again surrendered a single service break in the fourth set with Rafter then bringing up his first match point against the Frenchman's serve in the ninth game of the last set.
Pioline saved two match points against his serve in that game before an increasingly buoyant Rafter closed out the match in the following game on his fourth match point.
Australia's Mark Woodforde was due to meet Arnaud Boetsch in the second singles match later on Friday.
